_why: The allowance rule is written twice — once in Python for the screens, once in Go for the ingest door — and both say in comments that the two must agree. Nothing checked it. A divergence refuses a paying customer at a limit the screen never showed them, which is the failure the comments name and neither could prevent. These cases are read by apps/api/tests and by apps/receiver, so the agreement is a fact rather than an assertion (AC25.15, docs/features/usage-billing/spec.md).
_rule: A plan that caps the services it bills sets the count. A plan with no cap is sized on what the customer committed to. Neither present is null, which enforces nothing — deliberately not zero, which is a plan that includes nothing.

cases.name: the free tier caps at its own ceiling
the plan's own cap wins over a larger commitment
the plan's own cap wins over a smaller commitment too
a paying tier is sized on what the customer committed to
a paying tier with no active subscription enforces nothing
a cap of zero is a plan that includes nothing, not an absent cap
a commitment of zero is likewise a statement, not an absence
